title: Writer and Present lose their native application menus
observation: Live AX trees expose only the app menu for Writer/Present; their document menus appear inside the window. Sheets exposes native File/Edit/View/Table/Window/Help. Writer/Present install Loom menus before showing the window, but leave Slint 1.17.1’s default menu enabled. The backend installs its app-only default menu on activation. Sheets explicitly disables that default first.
recommendation: Reuse Sheets’ backend initialization for Writer and Present. Retain the same command IDs, enable/checked state and handlers. Suppress the local menu only after a real native menu is installed and survives window activation.
check: Activate each app, open File/Edit/View in the macOS menu bar, invoke New/Undo/Save, switch apps and return, and repeat with multiple document windows. Confirm menus and shortcut state remain correct.

title: Native macOS frame and client chrome are visually disjoint
observation: The later owner screenshot shows native traffic lights and document titles for Sheets and Present. It disproves a blanket assertion that decorations never exist. It also shows a strong visual break between the native titlebar and Loom’s opaque client toolbar. The cropped image cannot establish actual NSWindow/content bounds or a backing-scale mismatch. Current code requests native frames by default; the custom-chrome environment path remains unsupported on macOS.
recommendation: Retain functional native controls and establish coherent titlebar/client hosting. Measure frame, content, logical and physical bounds before diagnosing DPI or resizing. Review an appropriate native macOS titlebar/material adapter while preserving the Rust/Slint architecture.
check: At equal logical client sizes on native 1×/2×, record OS frame/content bounds, backend inner physical size and scale factor; move between displays, resize and exercise traffic lights/drag/full screen. Compare active/inactive titlebar and client chrome, including standard versus custom-chrome launch paths.

title: No explicit Liquid Glass or native-material integration
observation: The searched desktop/UI/application sources have no explicit NSGlassEffectView, NSVisualEffectView or vibrancy/material adapter; their shared surfaces are opaque Slint colour fills. The resulting shell does not adopt current macOS material hierarchy. The supplied and live Apple 14.5 references are useful for layout, but cannot establish current Liquid Glass appearance.
recommendation: Investigate an OS-gated Rust/AppKit material adapter around the existing Slint host and chrome; feasibility with the current renderer must be proven first. Keep Loom’s identity, menus and document engines. Apply materials to controls/navigation, preserve opaque document artwork, and honor Reduce Transparency, Increase Contrast and Reduce Motion. A generic translucent rectangle is not native Liquid Glass.
check: Compare a native macOS window over contrasting backgrounds, in active/inactive states, light/dark, reduced transparency/contrast/motion and older-OS fallback. Verify document pixels and export content remain unchanged.

title: Template preview and created document disagree
observation: Selecting Blank Black and Create Document produced a white page with the status “Created blank black document.” The source routes Blank and BlankBlack through the same blank_document. Newsletter’s thumbnail depicts columns while its creation path emits sequential blocks. The existing UI-12 FIXED record needs review against this current evidence.
recommendation: Create preview and document from the same descriptor; remove misleading visual promises until the document supports them.
check: Create every offered template, compare actual page geometry/content with its preview, then Save/Open and independently inspect an export.

title: Typography lacks direct numeric entry
observation: Font size is a text display between +/- buttons, stepped by one point. The Pages reference exposes a typed size field with a pt unit. Preset margins also prevent exact custom page geometry.
recommendation: Reuse a shared validated numeric field with units, Enter/Escape and a single undo transaction; retain steppers. Avoid inventing a separate app-local control.
check: Enter an exact size, reject invalid input visibly, cancel without changes, undo one committed edit, save/reopen. Define supported fractional sizes explicitly.

title: Inspector hierarchy gives specialist controls too much prominence
observation: Paragraph Direction precedes common style/font controls; superscript/subscript and logical alignment take permanent rows. Document comments precede Page Setup in one long scroll area. Common settings become less direct than in Pages, especially as comments accumulate.
recommendation: Put current style, family, size and common formatting first. Group direction/baseline options into secondary disclosures; give comments a distinct review region and keep Page Setup stable.
check: Test typical text formatting and page setup with many comments at 1024x720 and 1280x800, with keyboard navigation and a compact drawer.

title: Page-position text is hardcoded
observation: The Document inspector’s visible and accessible summary says Page 1 of N even though the app tracks visible pages separately.
recommendation: Use “N pages” for a document summary, or derive current page from a clearly defined caret/viewport policy.
check: Move to page 3 in a multipage document; check visible and accessible position before and after scrolling and editing.

title: Charts appear as summary cards rather than plotted document content
observation: Chart projection draws a title and a textual type/category/series summary in a fixed-height card. Insert Chart consumes clipboard chart data. The editor cannot communicate the actual plotted shape of that data while composing.
recommendation: Render the actual chart using shared document geometry; label the clipboard-only source honestly until direct chart creation exists.
check: Copy a real chart from Sheets, inspect its page rendering, undo/save/reopen, and independently inspect PDF/DOCX fidelity. This flow was not run in this audit.

title: Clipboard/export failures need readable feedback
observation: Some text-copy branches report success only and leave clipboard-write failures silent. DOCX export appends consequential omitted-comment warnings after the destination path in an eliding status line; actual truncation was not reproduced.
recommendation: Report copy errors visibly. Put export losses before paths and provide readable details rather than relying on a single eliding line.
check: Inject clipboard write failure and verify visible feedback without content loss; export a relevant commented document to a long path at compact width and inspect all loss details.

title: Zoom omits current scale and a direct fit action
observation: The toolbar label is only Zoom. Its menu exposes In/Out/Actual Size without a visible percentage or Fit Width/Fit Page. At large sizes the page remains narrow within a broad surround.
recommendation: Expose current percentage and fit actions based on real document and viewport geometry.
check: Resize with inspector open/closed, select fit modes and manual zoom, and verify caret/hit/selection alignment at each scale.

title: Property search cannot find visible font controls
observation: Typing font in Search returns “No matching properties”; clearing it reveals Font Style and Font size. The keyword lists omit font/bold/fill/wrap/alignment/decimals.
recommendation: Match actual property labels and reveal the relevant section/tab.
check: Search each visible property name, use the resulting control by keyboard, clear the query and retain the expected selection.

title: Data-format labels and actions disagree
observation: The 123 choice is named Number but dispatches General. The 1.23 choice is named Decimal places but dispatches Number; decimals already have a separate stepper.
recommendation: Align visible labels, accessible names, selected state and the actual command with General/Number/Currency/Percent.
check: Choose each format on numeric cells; verify rendered output, accessibility name/state and saved format.

title: Inspector repeats metadata and delays editable controls
observation: Selection/Value/Formula wells repeat the grid/name/formula bar before formatting. At 1280x800 Data Format reaches the bottom; alignment and dimensions require scrolling. At 1440x900 they remain below the fold.
recommendation: Collapse repeated cell information and move editable properties upward. Keep the current restrained grid and toolbar.
check: Perform size, number-format and alignment tasks at 1280x800 without hunting through metadata; retain accessible labels and focus.

title: Exact cell geometry cannot be typed
observation: Font size, decimals, row height and column width use non-editable values with +/- controls. Width steps by 10px and height by 4px. Numbers’ reference has typed, unit-labelled fields.
recommendation: Use shared numeric entry with units and validation, preserving one undo step and the existing steppers.
check: Enter exact width/height/size, cancel an invalid edit, undo, save/reopen and verify document geometry.

title: Insert Chart reuses the existing chart without saying so
observation: With an existing chart, a second insertion overwrites its source while retaining its prior title/type, then reports Inserted. This is undoable; no irreversible loss is claimed.
recommendation: Within the one-chart model, label the operation Change Chart Source and identify the changed range. Do not add multi-chart architecture just to fix this wording.
check: Create chart A, select range B, invoke the action, verify truthful wording/title/source and undo restoration.

title: Table name actually renames the worksheet
observation: The Table name field dispatches rename_sheet, changes the sheet tab and updates cross-sheet formulas. Loom’s worksheet grid is distinct from Numbers’ separate table objects.
recommendation: Call the field Worksheet name and the section Worksheet. Keep the current model explicit.
check: Rename a sheet referenced by another sheet, verify the tab/formula update and undo, and confirm all visible terminology agrees.

title: Chooser locale looks interactive but has no operation
observation: The English (US) footer includes a dropdown chevron without an input/callback. This repeats an Apple chooser affordance without its behavior.
recommendation: Remove the chevron or footer until locale selection has real semantics.
check: Every enabled-looking chooser control is keyboard-operable and changes a meaningful setting, or is rendered as plain information.

title: Unchecked toggle menu items lose checkability
observation: Toolbar menu item checkable is derived from checked; an unchecked toggle is no longer exposed as a checkable command.
recommendation: Declare toggle/radio semantics independently of current checked state.
check: Inspect native accessibility trees for Bold and appearance options in both on/off states. No spoken output claim from source.

title: Text and fill swatches are skipped by keyboard navigation
observation: From Selected element text, the native Tab sequence traversed size, bold, italic and alignment, then jumped directly to X/Y/Width/Height/Rotation. Every text-colour and fill swatch was skipped. Source swatches lack focus/key handling; their names are ordinal “Text colour 1” / “Fill 1”.
recommendation: Reuse a shared focusable colour control with arrow navigation, Space/Enter activation, visible focus and actual colour names.
check: Complete text/fill colour changes and undo without a pointer, with visible focus and meaningful accessible names in all themes.

title: Geometry strips unit suffixes without conversion
observation: X/Y/Width/Height labels omit units. The parser removes arbitrary alphabetic suffixes, so 2 in becomes the scene value 2 rather than two inches. Runtime was not exercised.
recommendation: Show the supported unit; accept only defined suffixes with real conversion and reject unsupported ones visibly.
check: Try supported values, 2 in, unknown suffixes, invalid/nonfinite numbers; verify expected geometry, error feedback and undo.

title: Multi-selection style and geometry behave differently
observation: Style applies to all selected styleable objects; typed geometry finds the first selected object only, while the inspector retains singular wording.
recommendation: Make the selection scope explicit. Apply coherent group geometry or disable single-object geometry until one object is selected.
check: Select two objects, change style and geometry, verify visible scope/mixed state and one-step undo.

title: Morph is an enabled fade fallback
observation: Animate offers Morph alongside Dissolve/Push, but all non-Push effects share an opacity animation without object correspondence. This does not supply the distinctive behavior that the label teaches users to expect.
recommendation: Expose truthful existing effects; hide Morph until its defining behavior is implemented.
check: Use two slides with a matching moved/resized object and verify the named effect visually in playback, including reduced motion.

title: Editor zoom and slideshow fit share state
observation: Only Fit/75%/50% are available; preview remains bound to editor zoom and preview toggle does not reset it. The native fullscreen captures in this audit were blank and cannot safely distinguish rendering from capture behavior, so the specific fit defect is not declared runtime-confirmed.
recommendation: Separate editing zoom from presentation fit and verify playback independently of window-capture behavior. Add useful editing magnification as a bounded follow-up.
check: Set 50%, Play on a real display, compare Fit playback and slide corners; return to editing without losing the chosen editor zoom.

title: Inspector consumes space while duplicating modes
observation: Format/Animate/Document appear in both toolbar and inspector tabs. With no object selected the inspector is mostly empty. Opening it at 1280px makes the slide narrower than at 1024px with the panel closed.
recommendation: Keep one mode selector; use a user-controlled contextual inspector and a stable workspace as the window changes size.
check: Resize 1024→1280→1440 with panel state preserved; verify common editing controls remain reachable and the slide fits.

title: High contrast changes slide artwork colours
observation: The sample subtitle is gray in light/dark and black in high contrast. Rendering uses theme paper-muted for document text. This is a visible document change, not an export-byte result.
recommendation: Separate document-owned colours from application appearance, while retaining accessible chrome and selection affordances.
check: Switch app appearance on the same deck and compare document-only pixels and independently inspected export content.

title: Themes are layouts; chart insertion hides its prerequisite
observation: Chooser options generate placeholder arrangements rather than stored visual font/palette/background identities; previews use text descriptions. Chart invokes clipboard import and reports the Sheets prerequisite only after it fails. Text has one style per whole element and no font-family picker.
recommendation: Use real layout miniatures, distinguish layout from theme, and name the current command Paste Chart from Sheets. Treat richer document themes/typography as a separate capability scope.
check: Create each layout and compare preview/content; invoke chart with/without valid clipboard data; preserve an existing deck when changing document settings.

title: Palette advertises the wrong Add Slide shortcut
observation: The palette says Ctrl+Shift+A; the handler and menu use Ctrl+Shift+N.
recommendation: Derive shortcut labels from the shared command registration.
check: Compare menu/palette labels and invoke the advertised shortcut with native keyboard input.

title: Light-theme menu hover has no visible colour change
observation: Both surface and surface-raised are #ffffff in Light. Local menu backgrounds use surface and ghost buttons/popup rows use surface-raised on hover. The event may fire correctly while the displayed fill remains identical.
recommendation: Use a distinct shared hover treatment that remains legible in every theme, with keyboard focus distinct from hover.
check: Move a real pointer across menu labels and popup rows, capture before/after, and repeat light/dark/high contrast. The available CUA API exposes no hover-only movement; source is not a substitute for this native pointer check.

title: Open menu state is ignored by the ghost paint branch
observation: Local menu labels pass selected=open-index, but the ghost-button paint branch runs before the selected branch and ignores it. An open menu has no persistent selected fill when hover/focus is absent.
recommendation: Make selected/open state an explicit supported state of the shared ghost menu label, using shared tokens.
check: Open File, move away from its label, switch keyboard focus and verify the active menu remains visibly marked until dismissal.

title: Open menus lack pointer switching and pointer/keyboard selection synchronization
observation: Top-level menu switching is click-only. Popup hover paints a row but never updates selected-index, so Enter can still activate the previous keyboard-selected row. Direct mouse activation has real command dispatch; the audit does not claim every menu command fails.
recommendation: Support the normal desktop open-menu pointer transition; synchronize pointer and keyboard selection while keeping disabled commands guarded and dismissal/focus restoration correct.
check: Click File then move across Edit/View without clicking; hover another enabled row then press Enter; verify indicated and invoked actions agree. Check safe click activation exactly once, disabled rows, outside click, Escape and return to document focus.

title: Toolbar focus/selection outlines have no vertical breathing room
observation: Sheets caps the toolbar at 48 logical px plus text scaling; shared labelled items have a 48 px minimum and 52 px maximum, while the toolbar supplies no vertical padding. Focus/selected outlines therefore fill the row height and meet the separators. Image’s 2px focus border and Format’s 1px selected border are different states of the same control. The separate 32px More button is an alignment boundary to measure; its precise offset is not proven by the crop.
recommendation: Define shared row/item geometry with a consistent vertical inset, icon/label baselines and unclipped accessible focus. Explicitly center compact overflow beside labelled items. Do not shrink targets or remove focus outlines.
check: At native 1×/2× and text scale1.0, measure control rectangles/insets and baselines; focus Image and More, toggle Format, resize and verify visible-center clicks and focus return. Distinguish this confirmed padding issue from an unmeasured backing-scale hypothesis.

title: Application identity is incomplete across distribution surfaces
observation: At audit start there were no canonical app-brand PNG/ICO/ICNS assets or main-window icon bindings. Linux packaging generated generic letter tiles; macOS packaging omitted CFBundleIconFile and icon resources, and Windows shortcuts/executables had no explicit app icon. Three original icons and platform encodings are now created. Source integration is a separate verified result; portable Windows PE embedding and native OS cache/display checks remain relevant gaps.
recommendation: Use one canonical asset family and provenance registry; wire Slint windows/presenter, native macOS bundle resources, existing Linux icon installation and Windows installer shortcuts. Track raw Windows executable embedding until validated on Windows.
check: Validate PNG alpha/dimensions, ICO size entries, ICNS round trip, actual packaging declarations/files and native Dock/Finder/taskbar/launcher identity after a fresh install/relaunch, at small and Retina sizes.
